subject: Network connectivity options for Finovate private deployment: Peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN
messages:

Subject: Connectivity options for Redwood Private deployment

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for taking this. We’re evaluating a Redwood Private deployment that will host inference for a customer-facing feature in our us-east-1 VPC. We need guidance on the tradeoffs between VPC Peering, AWS PrivateLink, and Site-to-Site VPN (and surface any Transit Gateway implications).

Quick constraints/requirements:
- No public internet egress for inference traffic (all traffic must remain private).
- Data residency: logs and raw payloads must remain in our account; we can forward aggregated metrics.
- Throughput: ~20 TB/mo outbound from our VPC to Redwood for model payloads.
- Latency target: p95 < 100ms for short inference calls (single-turn).
- Security: end-to-end encryption required; we can do mTLS at the application layer.
- Account boundaries: Redwood will be a separate AWS account (vendor-managed VPC).
- We already have a Transit Gateway attached to several VPCs for other services.

Can you give a practical recommendation (risks, cost roughs, implementation notes)? I attached a short constraints doc.

Thanks,
Alex

Hi Alex —

Appreciate the detail, and the constraints doc helped. Looping in Grace (platform product) and Kimberly (security) for the final recommendation.

Quick clarifying Qs before we draft the matrix:
1) Is the Finovate VPC in the same AWS account as the TGW you mentioned, and do you control that TGW attachments (i.e., can you accept a new attachment from Redwood)?
2) Are there any NAT/firewall appliances in the path that would affect MTU or protocol (some customers run a bunch of NGFWs on the TGW route table)?
3) Expected sustained concurrent TPS at peak (rough number) so we can size bandwidth and understand if VPN throughput is feasible.

Initial thinking (very high level):
- If both VPCs can attach to the same Transit Gateway and you can accept a new TGW attachment, TGW gives clean hub-and-spoke routing and simplifies multiregion/multi-account scale.
- VPC Peering is lowest-latency and cost-effective inside the same region/account but has limits across accounts and doesn't scale well for many spokes.
- PrivateLink (AWS NLB + VPC Endpoint Service) is great for cross-account private connectivity with stronger isolation and control over exposure; it has per-GB data processing costs and per-endpoint hourly costs. It adds an extra hop (ENI in the consumer VPC) which can affect source IP visibility.
- Site-to-site VPN is the fallback for on-prem or when you can't accept direct peering/PL; it's cheapest to stand up but higher-latency and harder to meet strict p95 targets without AWS Direct Connect or BGP-accelerated VPN options.

If you can answer the 3 Qs above I’ll put together a decision matrix with latency/cost/operational tradeoffs and a recommended hybrid pattern (we often propose PrivateLink for control/management APIs and TGW/peering for bulk low-latency inference data flows).

Would Monday morning CT work for a 30m sync?

—Rishi

Subject: RE: Connectivity options for Redwood Private deployment — recommended pattern

Alex / Finovate SRE + team —

Thanks for the answers and the call yesterday. We reviewed options and ran a short internal cost/latency estimate. Below is a concise recommendation, the reasoning, and next steps. I attached our decision matrix and an updated diagram.

Executive recommendation (hybrid):
- Use Transit Gateway attachment for bulk inference traffic between Finovate VPC(s) and Redwood Private VPC(s) to meet latency and scale targets.
- Expose control-plane endpoints (model registry, management APIs, telemetry ingest) via AWS PrivateLink (endpoint service in Redwood account + interface endpoints in Finovate). This preserves strict exposure controls and simplifies IAM/authorization on service endpoints.
- Use Site-to-Site VPN only for on-prem/remote sites or as an encrypted backup path; do not route primary inference traffic over standard internet VPN if p95 <100ms is a hard requirement.

Why this mix?
- Latency: TGW attachment within the same region typically gives lower p95 than VPN and fewer hops than PrivateLink for large bulk flows. For your peak (1k TPS) we expect TGW+ENI sizing to keep p95 within target (detailed numbers in the matrix).
- Isolation & security: PrivateLink provides tight cross-account control for the control plane; you get explicit whitelistable endpoints and reduced attack surface.
- Cost: PrivateLink incurs per-GB processing fees for control-plane traffic, but that traffic is low-volume so costs are modest. Bulk inference egress via TGW avoids per-GB PrivateLink fees (TGW has per-GB charges but usually lower at scale).
- Operational: TGW centralizes routing; because you already own a TGW and can accept attachments, it's the least operational friction for multi-VPC scale.

Implementation notes / prescriptive checklist:
- TGW attachment: Redwood will request an attachment from Finovate; confirm change window and provide the Redwood account ID and VPC CIDR ranges. We will request AWS Resource Access Manager acceptance if cross-account.
- Route tables: Add explicit routes for Redwood subnets in your TGW route table. Avoid overlapping CIDRs; if overlap exists we’ll recommend SNAT for transient ranges.
- MTU/MTU discovery: Keep MTU=1500 end-to-end; ensure the firewall appliance doesn’t alter MSS. We’ll enable TCP MSS clamping on the gateway if needed.
- Security groups & NACLs: Principle of least privilege. Open only the ports/protocols required for inference (HTTPS 443, mTLS ports). PrivateLink interface endpoints require security groups that allow inbound from your app subnets.
- Logging & auditing: Enable VPC Flow Logs on the Finovate spokes and TGW Flow Logs for troubleshooting. Configure mTLS at the application layer; we’ll also sign TLS certs from our CA and exchange public keys.
- Source IP visibility: PrivateLink will terminate at an ENI in the Finovate VPC so backend will see the ENI IP as source — if original client IP is required in logs, we’ll pass X-Forwarded-For at the application layer or use IP-preserving patterns when traffic is routed via TGW.

Rough cost tradeoffs (order-of-magnitude, region-dependent):
- TGW: hourly + per-GB (moderate at 20TB/mo). Good for bulk egress at your scale.
- PrivateLink: per-endpoint-hour + per-GB processing (cheap for low-volume control plane).
- VPN: minimal setup cost, per-GB over internet; expect higher latency and jitter; not recommended for primary inference traffic without Direct Connect.

Risks & mitigations:
- TGW single point: if TGW is a choke point, we’ll recommend autoscaling multi-attachment patterns and monitor bandwidth. Implement SLOs per route and fallback policies (PrivateLink fallback for control plane).
- Change window coordination: Network changes require your ops approval; we’ll provide a rollback plan and a preflight checklist.
- Audit/regulatory: We’ll provide the requested logs (flow + app-level) and an architecture diagram for your auditors.

Next steps / action items:
1) Finovate: confirm TGW attachment window + provide account ID & target VPC CIDRs.
2) Redwood: generate TGW attachment request and PrivateLink service configuration (we’ll share endpoint service name and NLB details).
3) Joint: schedule a 2-hour cutover/validation window; we will run traffic tests (latency + throughput) and validate flow logs.

Attachments: connectivity_decision_matrix.xlsx, redwood_network_diagram_v2.png

If this matches your expectations I’ll open a delivery ticket and draft the change window request.

—Rishi
